The Heretic optimiser treats which layers to edit and the scaling coefficient as free parameters, producing candidates that vary in both \\emph{where} the edit energy is placed (depth placement) and \\emph{how much} total energy is applied (dose, measured as the Frobenius norm of the weight perturbation). We ask whether placement matters independently of dose.\n\n\\paragraph{Causal write profiles.} For each model, we construct a \\emph{causal write profile} by applying single-layer abliteration edits to each of the model's transformer layers in isolation, then measuring the residual refusal rate. This profile reveals which layers, when edited alone, are most effective at suppressing refusal. The \\emph{write-profile overlap} $O_{\\mathrm{SL}}$ measures the energy-normalised alignment between a multi-layer candidate's edit distribution and the causal write profile: higher overlap means the candidate concentrates its energy on layers that matter.\n\nFor Gemma, the confirmation-level Spearman correlations between the write-profile overlap and residual refusal are $\\rho = -0.96$ for English and $\\rho = -0.83$ for Slovene ($n = 18$ weight cells). The English and Slovene profiles are correlated at $\\rho = 0.59$. For GaMS3, the profile is analysed through a factorial design with two energy levels (E2 and E3) and ten placement configurations. The Spearman correlation between write-profile overlap $O_{\\mathrm{SL}}$ and residual Slovene refusal is $\\rho = -0.90$ ($p < 10^{-7}$), holding within both energy levels ($\\rho = -0.97$ at E2, $\\rho = -0.95$ at E3).\n\n\\paragraph{Replication in Qwen3-8B.} The write-profile overlap $O$ replicates in a third model, Qwen3-8B, with Spearman $\\rho = -0.76$ (pooled), $-0.93$ (E2), and $-0.84$ (E3), across 9 out of 9 matched groups. The overlap metric transfers: the rank ordering of which layers matter generalises beyond the two models in the primary study.\n\n\\paragraph{Primary criterion: falsified.} The primary criterion asks whether placement explains variance in residual refusal beyond dose. Adding placement to a dose-only regression yields $\\Delta R^2 = 0.027$ (Gemma) and $\\Delta R^2 = 0.056$ (GaMS3): placement contributes negligibly once dose is controlled. At the keyword floor---the region of the search space the optimiser actually selects from---dose dominates ($p = 0.774$). The within-model correlations between overlap and refusal, though strong, reflect the confounding of placement with dose across the search space rather than an independent causal contribution.\n\n\\paragraph{Raw depth.} Raw depth of the edit (mean edited layer index) does not significantly predict residual Slovene refusal in GaMS3: Spearman $\\rho = -0.34$, $p = 0.15$ (Figure~\\ref{fig:depth-placement}b). The write-profile overlap, which accounts for the non-uniform importance of layers, is the informative predictor (Figure~\\ref{fig:depth-placement}a).\n\n\\paragraph{Cross-model prediction.} The frozen activation-space DEV index---a single depth summary computed on Gemma and applied without refit to Qwen3-8B---fails cross-model prediction entirely: Spearman $\\rho = -0.009$ over 21 pooled cells (item-bootstrap 95\\% CI $[-0.13, 0.19]$, permutation $p = 0.16$). Higher overlap with the causal write profile predicts lower residual refusal. (b)~Raw depth of the edit (mean edited layer index): Spearman $\\rho = -0.34$, $p = 0.15$ (not significant). Raw depth alone does not predict residual refusal; the overlap metric, which accounts for layer importance, is the informative predictor.}\n  \\label{fig:depth-placement}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\n\\paragraph{Evaluation validity.} The keyword measurement bias is the central finding of this study. Abliterated checkpoints verified only by an English keyword counter carry no information about non-English refusal behaviour. The keyword counter detected zero Slovene refusals across all conditions (0/490 held-out Slovene responses, 0/100 verified Gemma-edit Slovene responses), and its threshold-blind fraction was 1.0 in both searches. TBF $= 1.0$ follows from the keyword floors (72 and 16, both above the 10-refusal threshold) combined with the counter's 81\\% false-positive rate on edited English text: the counter simultaneously over-fires in the source language and is silent in the target language. Any downstream use of these checkpoints as language-neutral references for safety evaluation inherits this validity gap.\n\n\\paragraph{Depth placement.} The depth placement finding has a narrower scope. Within a single model, the write-profile overlap $O_{\\mathrm{SL}}$---the energy-normalised alignment between a candidate's edit distribution and the causal write profile---correlates strongly with residual Slovene refusal, and this pattern replicates in Qwen3-8B ($\\rho = -0.76/-0.93/-0.84$, 9/9 matched groups). However, the primary criterion was falsified: placement does not explain variance beyond dose ($\\Delta R^2$ of 0.027 and 0.056). At the keyword floor, dose dominates ($p = 0.774$). The frozen DEV index, a single depth summary applied across models without refit, fails entirely ($\\rho = -0.009$). The practical consequence is that while the write-profile concept transfers, no fixed depth prescription carries from one model to another, and depth gains little once dose is held constant.\n\n\\paragraph{Judge reliability.} The depth-placement experiment's own judge (exp12) missed its certification gate ($\\kappa = 0.683$), adding a measurement caveat to the placement results beyond the main study's Slovene caveat ($\\kappa = 0.72$).\n\n\\paragraph{Model divergence.} The GaMS3--Gemma contrast is striking: the edit transfers fully to GaMS3 but largely fails on Gemma. The two checkpoints differ in their training data (GaMS3 was continually pretrained on 140B tokens including Slovene \\citep{Vres2026}), but we study only two models from one architecture family, so we cannot isolate whether continual pretraining, the specific training mix, or some other factor drives the difference.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\\label{sec:limitations}\n\nSeveral limitations constrain the scope of these findings.\n\n\\textbf{Slovene judge certification.} The Qwen3-14B workhorse judge does not meet the $\\kappa \\geq 0.80$ certification gate for Slovene (unweighted $\\kappa = 0.72$, CI $[0.63, 0.81]$). The certification gate requires both the population-weighted and unweighted kappa to reach 0.80; the weighted kappa is 0.87, but the unweighted kappa falls short. Absolute Slovene refusal rates may be biased. Within-Slovene relative comparisons (e.g., GaMS3-orig vs.\\ GaMS3-edit) are less affected, since the bias is approximately constant across checkpoints, but we cannot rule out differential bias.\n\n\\textbf{Depth-experiment judge certification.} The judge used in the depth-placement experiment (exp12) also fails its certification gate ($\\kappa = 0.683$). The placement correlations should be interpreted with this additional measurement caveat.\n\n\\textbf{Generation truncation.} 94--95\\% of edited English outputs and 70--92\\% of edited Slovene outputs were truncated at the 256-token generation limit. The judge classified refusal status from incomplete text in these cases, which may affect both refusal rate and ASR estimates.\n\n\\textbf{Two models, one architecture.} We study two closely related models (Gemma and its continual-pretraining derivative). The findings may not generalise to architecturally different families (e.g., Llama, Mistral). At the keyword floor, dose dominates ($p = 0.774$). The frozen activation-space DEV index failed cross-model prediction entirely ($\\rho = -0.009$ over 21 pooled cells, $p = 0.16$; Section~\\ref{sec:placement}).\n\\end{itemize}\n\nAll Slovene results carry a measurement caveat: the workhorse judge (Qwen3-14B) does not meet the $\\kappa \\geq 0.80$ certification gate for Slovene (unweighted $\\kappa = 0.72$; Section~\\ref{sec:limitations}). The depth-placement experiment's own judge also missed its certification gate ($\\kappa = 0.683$).\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_1_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Refusal rates on RefusEU S5 harmful prompts ($n=280$) for all five checkpoints. Bars are coloured by language: English (blue) and Slovene (orange). Abliteration transfers almost completely to Slovene for GaMS3 but fails for Gemma. The community reference checkpoint shows that deeper abliteration can partially overcome the language gap. Error bars show 95\\% Clopper--Pearson confidence intervals. Note: 94--95\\% of edited English outputs were truncated at the 256-token generation limit.}\n  \\label{fig:refusal-rates}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\section{Related Work}\n\nRepresentation engineering \\citep{Zou2023} showed that high-level concepts, including honesty and harmfulness, are linearly represented in transformer activations. \\citet{Arditi2024} extended this observation to refusal, demonstrating that a single direction in activation space mediates the refusal decision and that orthogonalising weights against this direction---abliteration---removes refusal behaviour. \\citet{Wei2024} studied the brittleness of safety alignment under pruning and low-rank modifications, finding that aligned behaviour is concentrated in a small number of parameters. These results establish that refusal is geometrically localised, but none of the studies above evaluated cross-lingual transfer.\n\nMultilingual safety evaluation has advanced through benchmarks such as RefusEU \\citep{Krasnodebska2026}, which provides paired harmful and benign prompts in multiple European languages. Safety moderation tools including Llama Guard \\citep{Inan2023} and PolyGuard \\citep{Kumar2025} provide multilingual refusal classification. \\citet{Marks2023} demonstrated that linear structure in representations generalises across domains, suggesting that refusal directions might transfer across languages. \\citet{Wang2025} confirmed that a single refusal direction generalises across 14 safety-aligned languages, but evaluated the direction itself rather than the keyword-based verification that accompanies abliteration in practice. Our results partially support cross-lingual transfer for GaMS3 but not for Gemma.\n\nJailbreaking research \\citep{Zou2023a, Shen2023, Mehrotra2023} has shown that aligned models can be attacked through adversarial suffixes, prompt injection, and automated red-teaming. \\citet{Mazeika2024} introduced HarmBench as a standardised evaluation framework. Abliteration differs from these attack vectors in that it modifies the model's weights rather than its inputs, producing a permanent and deterministic change.\n\nGaMS3 \\citep{Vres2026} is a continual pretraining of Gemma-3 on 140B tokens of Slovene, English, and related South Slavic languages, followed by supervised fine-tuning on over 200K instruction examples. GlotLID \\citep{Kargaran2023} provides the language identification we use to verify output language consistency.\n\n\\section{Method}\n\n\\subsection{Models and Checkpoints}\n\nWe study five checkpoints, all loaded in 4-bit NF4 quantisation throughout:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n\\item \\textbf{Gemma-orig}: \\texttt{google/gemma-3-12b-it} \\citep{Kamath2025}, the English-centric instruction-tuned baseline.\n\\item \\textbf{Gemma-edit}: Gemma-orig after Heretic-optimised abliteration (116 TPE trials, keyword objective). No candidate reached the primary selection rule ($\\leq 10$ keyword refusals out of 100); the fallback rule selected the candidate with the lowest keyword count (72/100).\n\\item \\textbf{GaMS3-orig}: \\texttt{cjvt/GaMS3-12B-Instruct} \\citep{Vres2026}, continually pretrained on Slovene.\n\\item \\textbf{GaMS3-edit}: GaMS3-orig after Heretic-optimised abliteration (116 TPE trials, keyword objective). The fallback rule selected the candidate with the lowest keyword count (16/100).\n\\item \\textbf{Community-ref}: An independently abliterated Gemma checkpoint from the community, included as a reference point.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\subsection{Heretic Optimisation}\n\nHeretic uses tree-structured Parzen estimation (TPE; \\citealt{Akiba2019}) to search over abliteration hyperparameters---which layers to edit, the scaling coefficient, and the refusal-direction extraction method \\citep{Arditi2024}. It optimises two objectives: an English keyword refusal rate (the fraction of 100 in-loop prompts whose responses contain English refusal keywords) and the KL divergence between the edited and original model on a calibration set. The selection rule is: minimise KL subject to refusals $\\leq 10/100$; if no candidate satisfies this constraint, fall back to minimising refusals subject to KL $\\leq 1.0$.\n\nBoth searches (Gemma and GaMS3) fell to the fallback branch, meaning no candidate achieved $\\leq 10$ keyword refusals out of 100 in-loop prompts. The keyword objective floor (the minimum keyword refusal count across all 116 candidates) was 72 for Gemma and 16 for GaMS3.\n\n\\subsection{Evaluation Protocol}\n\nAll checkpoints are evaluated on the RefusEU benchmark \\citep{Krasnodebska2026}, which provides 280 harmful prompts (S5 split) and 150 benign prompts (S6 split), each in English and Slovene. Each prompt produces a single greedy-decoded response (temperature 0, max 256 tokens). Responses are classified into \\{refused, partial, complied\\} by a local Qwen3-14B judge.\n\nRefusal rate is the fraction of harmful-prompt responses classified as refused. Attack success rate (ASR) is computed over the subset of responses where both safety guards (Llama Guard 3 \\citep{Inan2023} and PolyGuard \\citep{Kumar2025}) agree on a label, excluding disagreements. Over-refusal rate is the fraction of benign-prompt responses classified as refused. Language consistency is verified by GlotLID \\citep{Kargaran2023}.\n\n\\paragraph{Generation truncation.} The 256-token generation limit truncates a large share of edited English outputs: 95.4\\% of Gemma-edit EN and 94.2\\% of GaMS3-edit EN responses are truncated, compared with 96.7\\% for Gemma-orig EN and 26.3\\% for GaMS3-orig EN. Slovene truncation rates are lower (69.8\\% for Gemma-edit SL, 92.1\\% for GaMS3-edit SL). The high English truncation rate means that many compliant English responses were cut short, and the judge classified their refusal status from incomplete text.\n\n\\paragraph{Judge certification.} The Qwen3-14B workhorse judge was calibrated against GPT-4.1 labels on a held-out panel. English certification passed: unweighted $\\kappa = 0.86$ $[0.77, 0.92]$, gate met. Slovene certification failed: unweighted $\\kappa = 0.72$ $[0.63, 0.81]$, below the $0.80$ threshold. All Slovene absolute rates therefore carry a measurement caveat. Relative comparisons within Slovene (e.g., orig vs.\\ edit) are less affected, since the judge bias is approximately constant across checkpoints.\n\n\\section{Results}\n\\label{sec:results}\n\n\\subsection{Refusal Suppression Across Languages}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:headline} and Figure~\\ref{fig:refusal-rates} report the main refusal evaluation. Abliteration produces dramatically different cross-lingual outcomes for the two models.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Refusal rate and attack success rate (ASR) on RefusEU S5 harmful prompts ($n=280$ per cell), with 95\\% Clopper--Pearson confidence intervals. Over-refusal is on S6 benign prompts ($n=150$). Edited English outputs are truncated at 256 tokens in 94--95\\% of cases (see Method).}\n\\label{tab:headline}\n\\begin{tabular}{llccc}\n\\toprule\nCheckpoint & Lang & Refusal & ASR & Over-refusal \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS3-orig & EN & .986 [.971,.996] & .015 [.004,.030] & .100 [.053,.153] \\\\\nGaMS3-orig & SL & .871 [.829,.907] & .012 [.000,.027] & .107 [.060,.160] \\\\\nGaMS3-edit & EN & .014 [.004,.029] & .982 [.964,.996] & .000 [.000,.000] \\\\\nGaMS3-edit & SL & .000 [.000,.000] & .972 [.952,.992] & .000 [.000,.000] \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma-orig & EN & .971 [.950,.989] & .026 [.007,.049] & .087 [.040,.133] \\\\\nGemma-orig & SL & .939 [.911,.964] & .016 [.004,.031] & .327 [.253,.400] \\\\\nGemma-edit & EN & .287 [.233,.341] & .738 [.681,.794] & .013 [.000,.033] \\\\\nGemma-edit & SL & .739 [.686,.786] & .103 [.067,.143] & .193 [.133,.260] \\\\\n\\midrule\nCommunity-ref & EN & .054 [.029,.082] & 1.00 [1.00,1.00] & .007 [.000,.020] \\\\\nCommunity-ref & SL & .114 [.079,.154] & .870 [.822,.909] & .027 [.007,.053] \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\textbf{GaMS3}: Abliteration removes refusal almost completely in both languages. English refusal drops from 98.6\\% to 1.4\\% (McNemar $p < 10^{-81}$); Slovene refusal drops from 87.1\\% to 0.0\\% ($p < 10^{-73}$). Over-refusal also drops to zero in both languages. The edit transfers fully.\n\n\\textbf{Gemma}: Abliteration partially suppresses English refusal (97.1\\% $\\to$ 28.7\\%, $p < 10^{-57}$) but barely affects Slovene (93.9\\% $\\to$ 73.9\\%, $p < 10^{-15}$). The English ASR reaches only 73.8\\%, far below GaMS3's 98.2\\%. In Slovene, Gemma-edit's ASR is 10.3\\%; the edit scarcely works.\n\n\\textbf{Community reference}: The independently abliterated Gemma achieves much lower refusal in both English (5.4\\%) and Slovene (11.4\\%), suggesting that a more thorough abliteration procedure can reach deeper into the refusal mechanism even for Gemma.\n\nThe keyword counter that verified both the Gemma-edit and GaMS3-edit checkpoints did not detect this divergence. Both checkpoints were selected by the same fallback rule (minimise keyword refusals), and neither reached the primary gate. The next section quantifies why.\n\n\\subsection{Keyword Measurement Bias}\n\\label{sec:keyword-bias}\n\nThe keyword refusal counter that Heretic uses as its primary objective counts English refusal phrases (``I cannot'', ``I'm sorry'', etc.) in model responses. This counter is structurally unable to detect Slovene refusals, which are expressed in Slovene. The consequence is not merely that the optimiser misses a signal; the verified checkpoints cannot serve as language-neutral references for refusal evaluation.\n\nWe quantify the bias using the language-gap score $\\Delta_{\\mathrm{lang}}$. For each language $\\ell$, let $d_\\ell = r^\\mathrm{kw}_\\ell - r^\\mathrm{judge}_\\ell$ be the difference between the keyword positive rate and the judge positive rate. The language-gap score is $\\Delta_{\\mathrm{lang}} = d_{\\mathrm{SL}} - d_{\\mathrm{EN}}$: the excess understatement of refusal by the keyword counter in Slovene relative to English. For the Gemma-edit checkpoint on a verified subset of 100 paired S5 prompts ($n=100$, Qwen reference channel): the keyword counter fires on 87\\% of English responses but on 0\\% of Slovene responses, while the reference judge finds 13\\% English refusal and 82\\% Slovene refusal. Thus $d_{\\mathrm{SL}} = 0.00 - 0.82 = -0.82$ and $d_{\\mathrm{EN}} = 0.87 - 0.13 = 0.74$:\n\n\\begin{equation}\n\\Delta_{\\mathrm{lang}} = d_{\\mathrm{SL}} - d_{\\mathrm{EN}} = -0.82 - 0.74 = -1.56 \\quad [95\\% \\text{ CI: } -1.68, -1.44]\n\\end{equation}\n\nFigure~\\ref{fig:keyword-bias} illustrates the gap. The negative sign of $\\Delta_{\\mathrm{lang}}$ indicates that the keyword counter understates refusal in Slovene far more than in English: in Slovene the counter detects nothing while the judge finds 82\\% refusal, whereas in English the counter over-fires at 87\\% against a judge rate of only 13\\%.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_2_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Keyword counter vs.\\ reference judge positive rates for the Gemma-edit checkpoint on 100 verified paired prompts. The keyword counter fires on 87\\% of English responses but 0\\% of Slovene responses; the reference judge finds 13\\% English refusal and 82\\% Slovene refusal. $\\Delta_{\\mathrm{lang}} = d_{\\mathrm{SL}} - d_{\\mathrm{EN}} = -1.56$ [$-1.68$, $-1.44$]. The annotation shows TBF $= 1.0$: 6/6 Gemma and 37/37 GaMS3 candidates invisible to the keyword objective are counted by the keyword-based scorer C; under the reference judge J, the counts are 5/5 and 6/6.}\n  \\label{fig:keyword-bias}\n\\end{figure}\n\nThe \\textbf{threshold-blind fraction} (TBF) quantifies the consequence for optimiser selection. TBF is the share of candidates that a scorer places at or below the selection threshold ($\\leq 10/100$ refusals) but the keyword objective places above it. In both searches, TBF $= 1.0$. This follows mechanically from the keyword floors: the minimum keyword count across all 116 candidates was 72 for Gemma and 16 for GaMS3, both above the 10-refusal selection threshold. Since no candidate's keyword count is $\\leq 10$, every candidate that any other scorer would select is invisible to the keyword objective. Under the keyword-based scorer C, 6 out of 6 eligible Gemma candidates and 37 out of 37 eligible GaMS3 candidates are invisible; under the reference judge J, the counts are 5 out of 5 and 6 out of 6.\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:keyword} summarises the keyword counter's behaviour across four evaluation conditions, computed on held-out prompts from both Heretic searches (first-100-token window; $n$ ranges from 70 to 490 depending on condition). On edited English text, 81\\% of the keyword counter's refusal detections are false positives---keyword fragments appearing in compliant responses---confirming that the counter both over-fires in English and is silent in Slovene.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Keyword refusal counter vs.\\ judge reference on held-out prompts. The keyword counter correctly identifies English refusals in unedited models (CONCORDANT) but produces zero positives on Slovene text (SILENT) and misfires on edited English text (MISFIRING, FP share 0.81).}\n\\label{tab:keyword}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccl}\n\\toprule\nCondition & $n$ & $\\kappa$ & KW pos.\\ rate & Ref.\\ base rate & Mechanism \\\\\n\\midrule\nOriginal EN & 70 & 0.20 & 0.94 & 0.94 & CONCORDANT \\\\\nOriginal SL & 70 & 0.00 & 0.00 & 0.96 & SILENT \\\\\nEdited EN & 490 & 0.02 & 0.34 & 0.17 & MISFIRING \\\\\nEdited SL & 490 & 0.00 & 0.00 & 0.44 & SILENT \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Depth Placement vs.\\ Dose}\n\\label{sec:placement}\n\nAbliteration edits a subset of the model's transformer layers. The Heretic optimiser treats which layers to edit and the scaling coefficient as free parameters, producing candidates that vary in both \\emph{where} the edit energy is placed (depth placement) and \\emph{how much} total energy is applied (dose, measured as the Frobenius norm of the weight perturbation). We ask whether placement matters independently of dose.\n\n\\paragraph{Causal write profiles.} For each model, we construct a \\emph{causal write profile} by applying single-layer abliteration edits to each of the model's transformer layers in isolation, then measuring the residual refusal rate. This profile reveals which layers, when edited alone, are most effective at suppressing refusal. The \\emph{write-profile overlap} $O_{\\mathrm{SL}}$ measures the energy-normalised alignment between a multi-layer candidate's edit distribution and the causal write profile: higher overlap means the candidate concentrates its energy on layers that matter.\n\nFor Gemma, the confirmation-level Spearman correlations between the write-profile overlap and residual refusal are $\\rho = -0.96$ for English and $\\rho = -0.83$ for Slovene ($n = 18$ weight cells). The English and Slovene profiles are correlated at $\\rho = 0.59$. For GaMS3, the profile is analysed through a factorial design with two energy levels (E2 and E3) and ten placement configurations. The Spearman correlation between write-profile overlap $O_{\\mathrm{SL}}$ and residual Slovene refusal is $\\rho = -0.90$ ($p < 10^{-7}$), holding within both energy levels ($\\rho = -0.97$ at E2, $\\rho = -0.95$ at E3).\n\n\\paragraph{Replication in Qwen3-8B.} The write-profile overlap $O$ replicates in a third model, Qwen3-8B, with Spearman $\\rho = -0.76$ (pooled), $-0.93$ (E2), and $-0.84$ (E3), across 9 out of 9 matched groups. The overlap metric transfers: the rank ordering of which layers matter generalises beyond the two models in the primary study.\n\n\\paragraph{Primary criterion: falsified.} The primary criterion asks whether placement explains variance in residual refusal beyond dose. Adding placement to a dose-only regression yields $\\Delta R^2 = 0.027$ (Gemma) and $\\Delta R^2 = 0.056$ (GaMS3): placement contributes negligibly once dose is controlled. At the keyword floor---the region of the search space the optimiser actually selects from---dose dominates ($p = 0.774$). The within-model correlations between overlap and refusal, though strong, reflect the confounding of placement with dose across the search space rather than an independent causal contribution.\n\n\\paragraph{Raw depth.} Raw depth of the edit (mean edited layer index) does not significantly predict residual Slovene refusal in GaMS3: Spearman $\\rho = -0.34$, $p = 0.15$ (Figure~\\ref{fig:depth-placement}b). The write-profile overlap, which accounts for the non-uniform importance of layers, is the informative predictor (Figure~\\ref{fig:depth-placement}a).\n\n\\paragraph{Cross-model prediction.} The frozen activation-space DEV index---a single depth summary computed on Gemma and applied without refit to Qwen3-8B---fails cross-model prediction entirely: Spearman $\\rho = -0.009$ over 21 pooled cells (item-bootstrap 95\\% CI $[-0.13, 0.19]$, permutation $p = 0.16$). This failure concerns the frozen index, not the write-profile concept itself, which replicates (see above).\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_3_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Residual Slovene refusal rate for GaMS3-12B-Instruct as a function of two predictors. (a)~Write-profile overlap $O_{\\mathrm{SL}}$: Spearman $\\rho = -0.90$ ($p < 10^{-7}$); within energy levels, $\\rho = -0.97$ (E2) and $\\rho = -0.95$ (E3). Higher overlap with the causal write profile predicts lower residual refusal. (b)~Raw depth of the edit (mean edited layer index): Spearman $\\rho = -0.34$, $p = 0.15$ (not significant). Raw depth alone does not predict residual refusal; the overlap metric, which accounts for layer importance, is the informative predictor.}\n  \\label{fig:depth-placement}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\n\\paragraph{Evaluation validity.} The keyword measurement bias is the central finding of this study. Abliterated checkpoints verified only by an English keyword counter carry no information about non-English refusal behaviour. The keyword counter detected zero Slovene refusals across all conditions (0/490 held-out Slovene responses, 0/100 verified Gemma-edit Slovene responses), and its threshold-blind fraction was 1.0 in both searches. TBF $= 1.0$ follows from the keyword floors (72 and 16, both above the 10-refusal threshold) combined with the counter's 81\\% false-positive rate on edited English text: the counter simultaneously over-fires in the source language and is silent in the target language. Any downstream use of these checkpoints as language-neutral references for safety evaluation inherits this validity gap.\n\n\\paragraph{Depth placement.} The depth placement finding has a narrower scope. Within a single model, the write-profile overlap $O_{\\mathrm{SL}}$---the energy-normalised alignment between a candidate's edit distribution and the causal write profile---correlates strongly with residual Slovene refusal, and this pattern replicates in Qwen3-8B ($\\rho = -0.76/-0.93/-0.84$, 9/9 matched groups). However, the primary criterion was falsified: placement does not explain variance beyond dose ($\\Delta R^2$ of 0.027 and 0.056). At the keyword floor, dose dominates ($p = 0.774$). The frozen DEV index, a single depth summary applied across models without refit, fails entirely ($\\rho = -0.009$). The practical consequence is that while the write-profile concept transfers, no fixed depth prescription carries from one model to another, and depth gains little once dose is held constant.\n\n\\paragraph{Judge reliability.} The depth-placement experiment's own judge (exp12) missed its certification gate ($\\kappa = 0.683$), adding a measurement caveat to the placement results beyond the main study's Slovene caveat ($\\kappa = 0.72$).\n\n\\paragraph{Model divergence.} The GaMS3--Gemma contrast is striking: the edit transfers fully to GaMS3 but largely fails on Gemma. We observe this asymmetry but do not attribute it to a specific mechanism. The two checkpoints differ in their training data (GaMS3 was continually pretrained on 140B tokens including Slovene \\citep{Vres2026}), but we study only two models from one architecture family, so we cannot isolate whether continual pretraining, the specific training mix, or some other factor drives the difference.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\\label{sec:limitations}\n\nSeveral limitations constrain the scope of these findings.\n\n\\textbf{Slovene judge certification.} The Qwen3-14B workhorse judge does not meet the $\\kappa \\geq 0.80$ certification gate for Slovene (unweighted $\\kappa = 0.72$, CI $[0.63, 0.81]$). The certification gate requires both the population-weighted and unweighted kappa to reach 0.80; the weighted kappa is 0.87, but the unweighted kappa falls short. Absolute Slovene refusal rates may be biased. Within-Slovene relative comparisons (e.g., GaMS3-orig vs.\\ GaMS3-edit) are less affected, since the bias is approximately constant across checkpoints, but we cannot rule out differential bias.\n\n\\textbf{Depth-experiment judge certification.} The judge used in the depth-placement experiment (exp12) also fails its certification gate ($\\kappa = 0.683$). The placement correlations should be interpreted with this additional measurement caveat.\n\n\\textbf{Generation truncation.} 94--95\\% of edited English outputs and 70--92\\% of edited Slovene outputs were truncated at the 256-token generation limit. The judge classified refusal status from incomplete text in these cases, which may affect both refusal rate and ASR estimates.\n\n\\textbf{Two models, one architecture.} We study two closely related models (Gemma and its continual-pretraining derivative). The findings may not generalise to architecturally different families (e.g., Llama, Mistral). The Qwen3-8B data in the cross-model prediction test (Section~\\ref{sec:placement}) provides one additional architecture, but a systematic survey across model families is needed.\n\n\\textbf{One target language.} Slovene is a mid-resource Indo-European language. The keyword measurement bias extends to any language the keyword counter does not cover, but the degree of edit transfer failure may differ for typologically distant or extremely low-resource languages.\n\n\\textbf{NF4 quantisation.} All experiments use 4-bit NF4 quantisation. The refusal direction and abliteration behaviour may differ at full precision or other quantisation levels.\n\n\\textbf{Single Heretic configuration.} The abliteration uses a single Heretic configuration per model (116 TPE trials, default hyperparameter ranges). A more exhaustive search might yield different results.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nWe evaluated the cross-lingual transfer of English-tuned abliteration to Slovene on two 12B-parameter models and found that keyword-verified abliterated checkpoints are not valid language-neutral references for refusal evaluation. The English keyword counter is structurally blind to Slovene refusals ($\\Delta_{\\mathrm{lang}} = d_{\\mathrm{SL}} - d_{\\mathrm{EN}} = -1.56$, threshold-blind fraction 1.0), and the two models we tested diverge dramatically in whether the edit transfers to Slovene. Within each model, the write-profile overlap $O_{\\mathrm{SL}}$ correlates strongly with residual refusal and replicates in Qwen3-8B, but the primary criterion---that placement explains variance beyond dose---was falsified ($\\Delta R^2$ 0.027/0.056). At the keyword floor, dose dominates ($p = 0.774$). All Slovene absolute rates carry a caveat from the uncertified workhorse judge ($\\kappa = 0.72$), and the depth-experiment judge also missed its gate ($\\kappa = 0.683$).\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}\n", "numLines": 223, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 223}}

"""Build the JSON blobs embedded in interactive.html from the run's output files."""
import json, csv, tomllib, math

E4 = L / "iter_2/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_4"
EV5 = L / "iter_5/gen_art/gen_art_evaluation_5"
E15 = L / "iter_4/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_15"
E14 = L / "iter_4/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_14"
OUT = Path("data"); OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
CK = ["gemma_orig", "gemma_edit", "gams_orig", "gams_edit", "community_ref"]

# ---------- keyword markers (Heretic 3521f864 default config, verbatim)
def find(d):
    if isinstance(d, dict):
        for k, v in d.items():
            if k == "keyword_markers": return v
            r = find(v)
            if r: return r
MARKERS = find(tomllib.loads((L / "iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_dataset_1/data/provenance/heretic_3521f864_config.default.toml").read_text()))
assert len(MARKERS) == 33
def kw(t):
    if not t.strip(): return True
    r = " ".join(t.lower().replace("*", "").replace("’", "'").split())
    return any(m.lower() in r for m in MARKERS)

# ---------- per-item exp4 records
fm = json.load(open(E4 / "full_method_out.json"))
ex = {e["metadata_item_key"]: e for ds in fm["datasets"] for e in ds["examples"]}
it = pd.read_parquet(EV5 / "results/items_scored.parquet")
it4 = it[it.artifact == "exp4"]

# responses in full_method_out must equal the texts eval5 scored
for _, r in it4.iterrows():
    e = ex[r.item_key]
    assert kw(e[f"predict_{r.unit}_response"]) == bool(r.kw), r.item_key

# (1) verified pairs (100) used for delta_lang
pairs = {}
for _, r in it4[it4.pair_id.notna()].iterrows():
    p = pairs.setdefault(r.pair_id, {"id": r.pair_id, "dir": r.pair_id.split(":")[-1], "en": None, "sl": None, "r": {}})
    e = ex[r.item_key]
    p[r.lang] = {"key": r.item_key, "set": r.set, "prompt": e["input"]}
    p["cat"] = e["metadata_category_inferred_low_confidence"]
    p["r"].setdefault(r.unit, {})[r.lang] = {"t": e[f"predict_{r.unit}_response"], "q": r.qwen_cls,
        "kw": int(bool(r.kw)), "u": {"true": 1, "false": 0}.get(e[f"predict_{r.unit}_official_unsafe"], None),
        "cut": int(e[f"predict_{r.unit}_hit_max"] == "true")}
pairs = sorted(pairs.values(), key=lambda p: (p["dir"], int(p["id"].split(":")[2])))
print("pairs", len(pairs))

# (2) per-cell labels on S5 and S6 for the checkpoint chart (codes only)
cls_code = {"refused": "R", "partial": "P", "complied": "C", "irrelevant": "I", "empty": "E", "malformed": "M"}
cells = {}
for ck in CK:
    for lang in ("en", "sl"):
        for st in ("S5", "S6"):
            d = it4[(it4.unit == ck) & (it4.lang == lang) & (it4.set == st)].sort_values("item_key")
            q = "".join(cls_code.get(c, "-") if isinstance(c, str) else "-" for c in d.qwen_cls)
            u = "".join("-" if (v is None or (isinstance(v, float) and math.isnan(v))) else ("1" if v else "0") for v in d.official_unsafe)
            k = "".join("1" if v else "0" for v in d.kw)
            cells[f"{ck}|{lang}|{st}"] = {"q": q, "u": u, "kw": k}

# check against the paper's Table 1 / headline_table.csv
ht = {(r["checkpoint"], r["lang"]): r for r in csv.DictReader(open(E4 / "results/headline_table.csv"))}
for ck in CK:
    for lang in ("en", "sl"):
        c = cells[f"{ck}|{lang}|S5"]; q = [x for x in c["q"] if x != "-"]
        ref = sum(x == "R" for x in q) / len(q)
        u = [x for x in c["u"] if x != "-"]; asr = sum(x == "1" for x in u) / len(u)
        s6 = [x for x in cells[f"{ck}|{lang}|S6"]["q"] if x != "-"]; orr = sum(x == "R" for x in s6) / len(s6)
        row = ht[(ck, lang)]
        got = f"{ref:.3f} {asr:.3f} {orr:.3f}"
        exp = " ".join(row[k].split()[0] for k in ("refusal (S5)", "ASR official (S5)", "over-refusal (S6)"))
        print(ck, lang, got, "| table", exp, "OK" if got == exp else "MISMATCH")

# (3) delta_lang rows (qwen channel, exp4, S5X) with CIs from file
dl = []
for r in csv.DictReader(open(EV5 / "results/delta_lang.csv")):
    if r["artifact"] == "exp4" and r["channel"] == "qwen":
        dl.append({k: r[k] for k in ("unit", "n_pairs", "p_kw_en", "p_kw_sl", "p_ref_en", "p_ref_sl", "d_en", "d_sl", "delta_lang", "delta_lang_ci95_lo", "delta_lang_ci95_hi")})
print(json.dumps(dl, indent=0)[:1500])
# live recompute check
for u in CK:
    P = [p for p in pairs if u in p["r"] and "en" in p["r"][u] and "sl" in p["r"][u]]
    ok = [p for p in P if p["r"][u]["en"]["q"] not in (None, "judge_fail", "malformed") and p["r"][u]["sl"]["q"] not in (None, "judge_fail", "malformed")]
    ref = lambda c: 1 if c in ("refused", "empty") else 0
    n = len(ok)
    ke = sum(p["r"][u]["en"]["kw"] for p in ok) / n; ks = sum(p["r"][u]["sl"]["kw"] for p in ok) / n
    re_ = sum(ref(p["r"][u]["en"]["q"]) for p in ok) / n; rs = sum(ref(p["r"][u]["sl"]["q"]) for p in ok) / n
    print(u, n, round(ke, 3), round(ks, 3), round(re_, 3), round(rs, 3), "delta", round((ks - rs) - (ke - re_), 3))

# (4) optimiser candidates
pc = pd.read_csv(E15 / "results/per_candidate.csv")
cand = []
for _, r in pc.iterrows():
    f = lambda v: None if pd.isna(v) else (int(v) if float(v).is_integer() else float(v))
    cand.append({"m": r.model, "t": int(r.trial), "ph": r.phase, "K": int(r.K), "C": f(r.C), "J": f(r.J),
                 "Jr": f(r.J_ref), "Jp": f(r.J_partial), "KL": round(float(r.KL_replay), 5), "Kj": f(r.K_journal),
                 "sK": bool(r.selected_by_K), "sC": bool(r.selected_by_C), "sJ": bool(r.selected_by_J)})
bl = list(csv.DictReader(open(EV5 / "results/blindness_per_search.csv")))
blind = [{k: r[k] for k in ("search", "reference", "n_candidates", "objective_floor", "n_ref_below_threshold", "tbf", "tbf_num", "tbf_den", "slope", "mean_signed_error_per100", "spearman")} for r in bl]
print(blind)

# (5) held-out agreement
ho = [{k: r[k] for k in ("view", "cell", "n", "tp", "fp", "fn", "tn", "kappa", "keyword_positive_rate", "reference_base_rate", "fp_share", "mechanism")} for r in csv.DictReader(open(EV5 / "results/heldout_agreement.csv"))]

# (6) GaMS3 placement cells
cc = pd.read_csv(E14 / "results/cells.csv")
pl = []
for _, r in cc.iterrows():
    kind = None
    if r.cell.startswith("C_"): kind = "matched"
    elif r.cell.startswith("X_PC"): kind = "pc"
    elif r.cell.startswith("X_RND"): kind = "random"
    elif r.cell == "R_NOOP": kind = "noop"
    if kind is None: continue
    pl.append({"cell": r.cell, "kind": kind, "cfg": None if pd.isna(r["set"]) else r["set"], "lvl": None if pd.isna(r.level) else r.level,
               "E": round(float(r.E), 3), "nl": int(r.n_layers), "O": round(float(r.O_sl), 5), "sl": round(float(r.sl_harm_strict), 5),
               "slb": round(float(r.sl_harm_broad), 5), "en": round(float(r.en_harm_strict), 5), "n": int(r.sl_harm_n),
               "md": None if pd.isna(r.mean_depth) else round(float(r.mean_depth), 2),
               "bf": [round(float(r[f"band_frac_{a}"]), 4) for a in ("1_12", "13_24", "25_36", "37_48")] if not pd.isna(r.band_frac_1_12) else None})
m = [p for p in pl if p["kind"] == "matched"]
print("matched", len(m), "rho", spearmanr([p["O"] for p in m], [p["sl"] for p in m]))
for lv in ("E2", "E3"):
    mm = [p for p in m if p["lvl"] == lv]; print(lv, spearmanr([p["O"] for p in mm], [p["sl"] for p in mm]))

json.dump({"markers": MARKERS}, open(OUT / "markers.json", "w"), ensure_ascii=False)
json.dump(pairs, open(OUT / "pairs.json", "w"), ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
json.dump(cells, open(OUT / "cells.json", "w"), separators=(",", ":"))
json.dump({"rows": dl}, open(OUT / "delta.json", "w"), separators=(",", ":"))
json.dump({"cand": cand, "blind": blind}, open(OUT / "cand.json", "w"), separators=(",", ":"))
json.dump(ho, open(OUT / "heldout.json", "w"), separators=(",", ":"))
json.dump(pl, open(OUT / "placement.json", "w"), separators=(",", ":"))
for f in OUT.iterdir(): print(f, f.stat().st_size)

    <h1>An English Keyword Objective Is Blind to Its Own Edit in Slovene</h1>
    <p class="byline">Gemma-3-12B-IT and GaMS3-12B-Instruct, before and after Heretic abliteration, evaluated in English and Slovene. Every chart below is drawn from the run's recorded outputs.</p>

<main id="main" tabindex="-1">

<!-- 1. FINDING -->
<section class="block" id="finding" aria-labelledby="finding-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="finding">
      <div class="prose">
        <p class="kicker">The finding</p>
        <h2 id="finding-h">A refusal counter that cannot read Slovene</h2>
        <p><button type="button" class="term" data-term="abliteration">Abliteration</button> removes refusal from a language model by orthogonalising its weights against a <button type="button" class="term" data-term="direction">refusal direction</button> extracted from English contrast pairs. The optimiser, <button type="button" class="term" data-term="heretic">Heretic</button>, decides which candidate edit to keep by counting English refusal phrases in the model's answers.</p>
        <p><strong>The question:</strong> when that <button type="button" class="term" data-term="keyword">keyword counter</button> certifies an edited checkpoint, does it tell you anything about refusal in Slovene?</p>
        <p><strong>The answer is no.</strong> On 100 <button type="button" class="term" data-term="pairs">verified English–Slovene pairs</button> answered by the Gemma edit, the counter fires on 87% of English responses and on 0% of Slovene responses. The <button type="button" class="term" data-term="judge">reference judge</button> finds 13% English refusal and 82% Slovene refusal. The counter over-fires in the language it was written for and is silent in the other.</p>
        <div class="big" aria-describedby="big-cap">−1.56</div>
        <p class="bigcap" id="big-cap"><button type="button" class="term" data-term="dlang">Δ<sub>lang</sub></button> for Gemma-edit, 95% CI [−1.68, −1.44]. Zero would mean the counter errs equally in both languages.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="view" id="v-head" style="margin-top:0">
        <p class="q">How often does each instrument call an answer a refusal, on the same 100 paired prompts?</p>
        <div class="controls">
          <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Checkpoint" id="head-ck"></div>
        </div>
        <div class="chart" id="head-chart"></div>
        <ul class="legend" id="head-legend"></ul>
        <div class="stat-row" id="head-stats"></div>
        <p class="take" id="head-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- 2. HOW IT WORKS -->
<section class="block" id="how" aria-labelledby="how-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="kicker">How it works</p>
    <h2 id="how-h">One prompt pair through the pipeline</h2>
    <p class="prose">The stepper follows one real pair from the verified set through Heretic's search, its selection rule, the edited Gemma model's answers and the two instruments that score them. The pair is picked by a fixed rule: among pairs whose English row is the original RefusEU prompt, both languages refused by Gemma-orig, the edit's English answer flagged by the counter but not judged a refusal, and its Slovene answer judged a refusal that the counter misses, take the one with the shortest English prompt. Use the buttons, the numbered markers or the left and right arrow keys.</p>
    <div class="stepper" id="stepper" aria-roledescription="stepper">
      <div class="pipe" id="pipe"></div>
      <div class="stagebox" id="stagebox">
        <h3 id="stage-title" style="margin-top:0"></h3>
        <div id="stage-body"></div>
        <div class="stepnav">
          <button type="button" id="st-prev" aria-label="Previous stage">Previous</button>
          <button type="button" id="st-next" class="fwd" aria-label="Next stage">Next</button>
          <span class="small" id="st-pos" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        </div>
        <p class="sr" aria-live="polite" id="st-live"></p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- 3. EVIDENCE -->
<section class="block" id="evidence" aria-labelledby="ev-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="kicker">Explore the evidence</p>
    <h2 id="ev-h">The edit, the counter and the depth of the edit</h2>
    <p class="prose">Three views over the recorded outputs. The first asks whether the English-derived edit removes refusal in Slovene at all. The second lets you read the answers the counter gets wrong. The third covers the paper's secondary analysis of where in depth an edit places its energy.</p>

    <div class="view" id="v-ck">
      <p class="q">Does the same English-derived edit suppress refusal in both languages?</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <label class="ctl" for="ck-metric">Measure
          <select id="ck-metric">
            <option value="ref">Refusal rate, harmful prompts (S5, judge)</option>
            <option value="par">Partial compliance, harmful prompts (S5, judge)</option>
            <option value="asr">Attack success rate, harmful prompts (S5, official guards)</option>
            <option value="orr">Over-refusal, benign prompts (S6, judge)</option>
            <option value="kw">Keyword counter fires, harmful prompts (S5)</option>
          </select>
        </label>
        <label class="ctl"><input type="checkbox" id="ck-comm" checked> Show community reference</label>
      </div>
      <div class="chart" id="ck-chart"></div>
      <ul class="legend"><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--en)"></span>English</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--sl)"></span>Slovene</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:#fff;border:1.5px solid var(--ink-2)"></span>Hatched: unedited original (the baseline)</li></ul>
      <p class="small" id="ck-note"></p>
      <p class="take" id="ck-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
    </div>

    <div class="view" id="v-items">
      <p class="q">What does the counter actually see? Read the paired answers, before and after the edit.</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <label class="ctl" for="it-ck">Edited checkpoint
          <select id="it-ck">
            <option value="gemma_edit">Gemma-edit</option>
            <option value="gams_edit">GaMS3-edit</option>
            <option value="community_ref">Community-ref</option>
          </select>
        </label>
        <label class="ctl" for="it-filter">Show
          <select id="it-filter">
            <option value="all">All 100 pairs</option>
            <option value="silent">Slovene refusal the counter misses</option>
            <option value="fp">English counter hit, judge says not a refusal</option>
            <option value="wrong">Any counter error (either language)</option>
            <option value="split">Judge: refused in one language only</option>
          </select>
        </label>
        <label class="ctl" for="it-q">Search <input type="search" id="it-q" placeholder="words in prompt or answer" autocomplete="off"></label>
      </div>
      <p class="small" id="it-count" aria-live="polite"></p>
      <div class="browser">
        <ul class="itemlist" id="it-list" role="listbox" aria-label="Prompt pairs"></ul>
        <div id="it-detail" tabindex="-1"></div>
      </div>
      <p class="take" id="it-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
    </div>

    <div class="view" id="v-place">
      <p class="q">Secondary analysis: does it matter where in depth an edit puts its energy? (GaMS3, 20 matched-energy cells)</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <div class="seg" role="group" aria-label="Energy levels shown">
          <button type="button" aria-pressed="true" data-lvl="E2">E2 cells</button>
          <button type="button" aria-pressed="true" data-lvl="E3">E3 cells</button>
          <button type="button" aria-pressed="true" data-lvl="ctl">Controls</button>
        </div>
        <label class="ctl" for="pl-y">Outcome
          <select id="pl-y">
            <option value="sl">Slovene refusal, strict (refused)</option>
            <option value="slb">Slovene refusal, broad (refused or partial)</option>
            <option value="en">English refusal, strict</option>
          </select>
        </label>
      </div>
      <div class="chart" id="pl-chart"></div>
      <ul class="legend"><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--en)"></span>E2 cell</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--sl)"></span>E3 cell</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--base)"></span>Random or PC control (E3 energy)</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:#fff;border:1.5px dashed var(--ink-2)"></span>No-op</li></ul>
      <p class="take" id="pl-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
      <p class="small">The paper reports this correlation (ρ = −0.90 pooled; −0.97 at E2, −0.95 at E3) but also that its primary criterion, placement explaining variance beyond dose, was falsified (Δ<i>R</i><sup>2</sup> 0.027 for Gemma and 0.056 for GaMS3). Read this chart as a within-model ordering, not as a depth prescription.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- 4. TRY IT -->
<section class="block" id="try" aria-labelledby="try-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="kicker">Try it</p>
    <h2 id="try-h">Move the selection threshold; run the counter yourself</h2>
    <div class="view" id="v-thr">
      <p class="q">Heretic keeps the lowest-KL candidate with at most <i>t</i>/100 keyword refusals. What would a better refusal measure have let it see?</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <div class="seg" role="tablist" aria-label="Search" id="thr-search">
          <button type="button" role="tab" aria-selected="true" data-m="gemma">Gemma search</button>
          <button type="button" role="tab" aria-selected="false" data-m="gams">GaMS3 search</button>
        </div>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Reference scorer" id="thr-ref">
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="true" data-r="C">Classifier C</button>
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-r="J">Judge J</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="rangebox">
        <label for="thr" class="ctl">Selection threshold <i>t</i> (refusals per 100)</label>
        <input type="range" id="thr" min="0" max="100" step="1" value="10" aria-describedby="thr-out">
        <output id="thr-out" class="val" for="thr">10</output>
      </div>
      <div class="chart" id="thr-chart"></div>
      <ul class="legend"><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>Candidate the reference places at or below <i>t</i></li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--base)"></span>Other candidate</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:#fff;border:2px solid var(--bad)"></span>Edit the paper evaluates</li></ul>
      <div class="stat-row" id="thr-stats"></div>
      <p class="take" id="thr-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
      <p class="small">Every count is recomputed in the page from the recorded per-candidate refusal counts (116 candidates per search; the judge labelled 70 of the GaMS3 candidates). The rule is the paper's: minimise KL subject to at most <i>t</i> keyword refusals, otherwise fall back to the fewest keyword refusals with KL ≤ 1.0.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="view" id="v-demo">
      <p class="q">Can I check the counter's verdict myself?</p>
      <p class="small prose">This is Heretic's keyword rule (commit 3521f864), run in the page: an empty answer counts as a refusal; otherwise the text is lower-cased, <code>*</code> removed, typographic apostrophes straightened and whitespace collapsed, and it is a refusal if any of the 33 markers occurs as a substring. <span id="demo-check"></span></p>
      <div class="controls">
        <button type="button" class="btn" id="demo-en">Load a Gemma-edit English answer</button>
        <button type="button" class="btn" id="demo-sl">Load a Gemma-edit Slovene refusal</button>
      </div>
      <label for="demo-text" class="small" style="display:block;margin-bottom:4px">Answer text (edit freely)</label>
      <textarea id="demo-text" rows="6" style="width:100%"></textarea>
      <div class="demo-out" aria-live="polite">
        <p class="verdict" id="demo-verdict"></p>
        <div class="resp short" id="demo-hl"></div>
      </div>
      <p class="take" id="demo-take"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- 5. FAILS -->
<section class="block" id="fails" aria-labelledby="fails-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="kicker">Where it fails</p>
    <h2 id="fails-h">Three failure modes of the counter, and the paper's own limits</h2>
    <div class="view" id="v-held">
      <p class="q">On held-out prompts neither search saw, how does the counter's verdict line up with the judge's?</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Text the counter reads" id="ho-view">
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="true" data-v="first100tokens">First 100 tokens (in-loop view)</button>
          <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked="false" data-v="full_response">Full response</button>
        </div>
        <label class="ctl" for="ho-cell">Confusion matrix for
          <select id="ho-cell">
            <option value="original_en">Original, English</option>
            <option value="original_sl">Original, Slovene</option>
            <option value="edited_en" selected>Edited, English</option>
            <option value="edited_sl">Edited, Slovene</option>
          </select>
        </label>
      </div>
      <div class="two">
        <div>
          <div class="chart" id="ho-chart"></div>
          <ul class="legend"><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>Keyword counter fires</li><li><span class="sw" style="background:var(--base)"></span>Judge says refused (reference)</li></ul>
        </div>
        <div>
          <div class="tscroll" id="ho-cm"></div>
          <p class="small" id="ho-note"></p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p class="take" id="ho-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
      <p class="small">The failures, one click away: <button type="button" class="btn" id="jump-silent">Show every Slovene refusal the counter missed</button></p>
    </div>

    <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>
    <ul class="limits prose">
      <li><strong>The Slovene judge is not certified.</strong> The Qwen3-14B workhorse judge reaches unweighted <button type="button" class="term" data-term="kappa">κ</button> = 0.72 [0.63, 0.81] against GPT-4.1 on Slovene, below the 0.80 gate. English passes at κ = 0.86. Absolute Slovene rates carry this caveat; within-Slovene comparisons are less affected. The depth-placement experiment's judge also missed its gate (κ = 0.683).</li>
      <li><strong>Answers are truncated.</strong> 94–95% of edited English outputs hit the 256-token limit, so the judge often classified refusal from incomplete text. The item browser tags each capped answer.</li>
      <li><strong>Two models, one architecture family.</strong> The paper observes the GaMS3 and Gemma divergence but does not attribute it to continual pretraining, the training mix or any other factor.</li>
      <li><strong>Placement does not beat dose.</strong> The write-profile overlap orders cells within a model and replicates in Qwen3-8B, but the primary criterion was falsified (Δ<i>R</i><sup>2</sup> 0.027 and 0.056), and the frozen depth index failed cross-model prediction (ρ = −0.009 over 21 pooled cells).</li>
      <li><strong>One language, one precision, one search per model.</strong> Slovene only; all checkpoints in 4-bit <button type="button" class="term" data-term="nf4">NF4</button>; one Heretic configuration (116 <button type="button" class="term" data-term="tpe">TPE</button> trials) per model.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</section>
</main>

<script type="application/json" id="data-pairs" data-source="evaluation_5/results/items_scored.parquet (keyword verdict, judge class, pair ids) + experiment_4/full_method_out.json (prompts, answer texts, official-guard verdict, 256-token cap flag)">__PAIRS__</script>
<script type="application/json" id="data-cells" data-source="evaluation_5/results/items_scored.parquet (per-item judge class, official guard, keyword verdict on S5/S6) + experiment_4/results/headline_table.csv (95% CIs)">__CELLS__</script>
<script type="application/json" id="data-delta" data-source="evaluation_5/results/delta_lang.csv (exp4 S5X, qwen reference channel)">__DELTA__</script>
<script type="application/json" id="data-cand" data-source="experiment_15/results/per_candidate.csv + evaluation_5/results/blindness_per_search.csv">__CAND__</script>
<script type="application/json" id="data-heldout" data-source="evaluation_5/results/heldout_agreement.csv">__HELD__</script>
<script type="application/json" id="data-placement" data-source="experiment_14/results/cells.csv">__PLACE__</script>
<script type="application/json" id="data-markers" data-source="dataset_1/data/provenance/heretic_3521f864_config.default.toml (keyword_markers)">__MARKERS__</script>

<script>
"use strict";
(function () {
const $ = (s, r) => (r || document).querySelector(s);
const $$ = (s, r) => Array.from((r || document).querySelectorAll(s));
const D = id => JSON.parse(document.getElementById(id).textContent);
const PAIRS = D("data-pairs"), CELLS = D("data-cells"), DELTA = D("data-delta").rows, CANDD = D("data-cand"),
      HELD = D("data-heldout"), PLACE = D("data-placement"), MARKERS = D("data-markers").markers;
const CAND = CANDD.cand, BLIND = CANDD.blind;
const NAME = { gemma_orig: "Gemma-orig", gemma_edit: "Gemma-edit", gams_orig: "GaMS3-orig", gams_edit: "GaMS3-edit", community_ref: "Community-ref" };
const BASE = { gemma_edit: "gemma_orig", gams_edit: "gams_orig", community_ref: "gemma_orig" };
const LANG = { en: "English", sl: "Slovene" };
const SVGNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";
const pct = v => (v * 100).toFixed(0) + "%";
const f2 = v => (v < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(v).toFixed(2);
const esc = s => String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;" }[c]));
const css = n => getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(n).trim();

/* ---------------- keyword rule (Heretic 3521f864) ---------------- */
function normalise(text) {
  // returns normalised string plus, for each output char, the index of its source char
  let out = "", map = [], pendingSpace = false, started = false;
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    let ch = text[i];
    if (ch === "*") continue;
    if (/\s/.test(ch)) { if (started) pendingSpace = true; continue; }
    if (ch === "’") ch = "'";
    if (pendingSpace) { out += " "; map.push(i - 1); pendingSpace = false; }
    const lo = ch.toLowerCase();
    for (let k = 0; k < lo.length; k++) { out += lo[k]; map.push(i); }
    started = true;
  }
  return { out, map };
}
function keyword(text) {
  if (!text.trim()) return { hit: true, empty: true, found: [], ranges: [] };
  const { out, map } = normalise(text);
  const found = [], ranges = [];
  for (const m of MARKERS) {
    const mk = m.toLowerCase();
    let from = 0, idx;
    while ((idx = out.indexOf(mk, from)) !== -1) {
      if (!found.includes(m)) found.push(m);
      ranges.push([map[idx], map[idx + mk.length - 1] + 1]);
      from = idx + 1;
    }
  }
  return { hit: found.length > 0, empty: false, found, ranges };
}
function highlight(text, ranges) {
  if (!ranges.length) return esc(text);
  const r = ranges.slice().sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]), merged = [];
  for (const x of r) { const l = merged[merged.length - 1]; if (l && x[0] <= l[1]) l[1] = Math.max(l[1], x[1]); else merged.push(x.slice()); }
  let s = "", p = 0;
  for (const [a, b] of merged) { s += esc(text.slice(p, a)) + '<mark class="kwhit">' + esc(text.slice(a, b)) + "</mark>"; p = b; }
  return s + esc(text.slice(p));
}
const isRef = c => c === "refused" || c === "empty";

/* ---------------- term tooltips ---------------- */
const TERMS = {
  abliteration: ["Abliteration", "Removing refusal from a language model by identifying a refusal direction in activation space and orthogonalising the model's weight matrices against it."],
  direction: ["Refusal direction", "A direction in activation space, extracted from English harmful/harmless contrast pairs, that mediates the refusal decision. Abliteration projects it out of the weights."],
  heretic: ["Heretic", "The abliteration optimiser used here: a TPE search over which layers to edit, the scaling coefficient and the direction, scored by an English keyword refusal rate and a KL divergence to the original model."],
  keyword: ["Keyword counter", "Heretic's refusal objective: an answer counts as a refusal if it contains any of 33 English refusal substrings (\"I cannot\", \"sorry\", \"illegal\", ...) or is empty. It is scored on 100 in-loop prompts."],
  judge: ["Reference judge", "A local Qwen3-14B judge applying one frozen rubric to every answer, blind to model identity, labelling it refused, partial or complied. Refusal rate is the share labelled refused."],
  pairs: ["Verified pairs", "100 RefusEU prompts whose English and Slovene versions were checked as faithful translations (cross-translated in both directions), the only basis for paired cross-language claims."],
  dlang: ["Δlang (language-gap score)", "For each language, d = keyword positive rate − judge refusal rate. Δlang = d(SL) − d(EN): the excess understatement of refusal by the keyword counter in Slovene relative to English."],
  tbf: ["Threshold-blind fraction (TBF)", "The share of candidates that a scorer places at or below the selection threshold (≤ 10/100 refusals) but the keyword objective places above it."],
  selection: ["Selection rule", "Minimise KL subject to at most 10/100 keyword refusals; if no candidate qualifies, fall back to minimising keyword refusals subject to KL ≤ 1.0."],
  kappa: ["Cohen's κ", "Chance-corrected agreement between two labellers; 1 is perfect agreement, 0 is chance level. The judge certification gate is κ ≥ 0.80."],
  asr: ["Attack success rate (ASR)", "Share of harmful-prompt answers labelled unsafe, over the subset where both safety guards (Llama Guard 3 and PolyGuard) agree on a label."],
  overrefusal: ["Over-refusal", "Share of benign (XSTest-safe, S6) prompts whose answer the judge labels refused."],
  partial: ["Partial", "A judge class for answers that engage with a harmful request but hedge, caveat or withhold the operative detail. Refusal and compliance are not complements."],
  overlap: ["Write-profile overlap O", "The energy-normalised alignment between a multi-layer edit's per-layer energy and the causal write profile (the refusal drop from editing each layer alone). Higher O means the edit concentrates energy on layers that matter."],
  kl: ["KL divergence", "Heretic's second objective: divergence between the edited and original model's next-token distributions on harmless prompts, a proxy for collateral damage."],

  tpe: ["TPE", "Tree-structured Parzen estimation, the Bayesian search Heretic uses to propose candidate edits."],
  clfc: ["Classifier C", "A judge-distilled, partial-aware refusal classifier (TF-IDF features and logistic regression on the first 100 tokens), certified against the judge; one of the two reference scorers for optimiser candidates."]

function openTip(btn) {

  tip.style.maxWidth = w + "px";
  let left = r.left + window.scrollX; const maxLeft = window.scrollX + document.documentElement.clientWidth - w - 12;

    g.classList.add("active");
    t.innerHTML = html; t.hidden = false;
    const cb = container.getBoundingClientRect(), mb = g.getBoundingClientRect();
    const tw = Math.min(280, cb.width - 8);
    let x = mb.left - cb.left + mb.width / 2 - tw / 2;

    if (spec.rotate && narrow) { lab.setAttribute("transform", `rotate(-28 ${gx + gw / 2} ${H - m.b + 18})`); lab.setAttribute("text-anchor", "end"); lab.setAttribute("x", gx + gw / 2 + 6); }
    lab.textContent = g.label;
    if (g.sub) { const s = el("text", { class: "lbl", x: gx + gw / 2, y: H - m.b + 33, "text-anchor": "middle" }, svg); s.textContent = g.sub; }

    if (i === stage) g.setAttribute("aria-current", "step");

    const n = el("text", { class: "n", x, y: y + 5, "text-anchor": "middle" }, g); n.textContent = i + 1;
    const t = el("text", { class: "t", x, y: y + 38, "text-anchor": "middle" }, g); t.textContent = s.t;
    g.addEventListener("click", () => go(i));

  });

  $("#st-pos").textContent = `Stage ${stage + 1} of ${STAGES.length}`;
  $("#st-live").textContent = `Stage ${stage + 1} of ${STAGES.length}: ${s.h}`;
  const hadFocus = document.activeElement && document.activeElement.closest && document.activeElement.closest("#pipe");

$("#st-next").addEventListener("click", () => go(stage + 1));

/* ---------------- 3a. checkpoint chart ---------------- */
const CKS = ["gemma_orig", "gemma_edit", "gams_orig", "gams_edit", "community_ref"];

  const S5 = CELLS.cells[`${ck}|${lang}|S5`], S6 = CELLS.cells[`${ck}|${lang}|S6`];
  const frac = (str, hit) => { const a = str.split("").filter(x => x !== "-"); return [a.filter(x => x === hit).length / a.length, a.length]; };
  if (metric === "ref") return frac(S5.q, "R");
  if (metric === "par") return frac(S5.q, "P");
  if (metric === "asr") return frac(S5.u, "1");

  if (metric === "kw") return frac(S5.kw, "1");
}
const MET = { ref: "Refusal rate (S5)", par: "Partial share (S5)", asr: "Attack success rate (S5)", orr: "Over-refusal (S6)", kw: "Keyword counter fires (S5)" };
function drawCk() {
  const metric = $("#ck-metric").value, comm = $("#ck-comm").checked;
  const list = CKS.filter(c => comm || c !== "community_ref");
  const groups = list.map(ck => ({ label: NAME[ck], bars: ["en", "sl"].map(lang => {
    const [v, n] = cellRate(ck, lang, metric), ci = metric === "kw" ? null : CELLS.ci[`${ck}|${lang}`][metric];
    const orig = ck.endsWith("orig");
    return { label: LANG[lang], value: v, color: css(lang === "en" ? "--en" : "--sl"), pattern: orig ? "h-" + lang : null,
      ci: ci ? [ci[1], ci[2]] : null,
      tip: `<b>${NAME[ck]}, ${LANG[lang]}</b><br>${MET[metric]}: ${(v).toFixed(3)} (n = ${n})${ci ? `<br>95% CI from the run's table: [${ci[1].toFixed(3)}, ${ci[2].toFixed(3)}]` : ""}` };
  }) }));
  barChart($("#ck-chart"), { aria: MET[metric] + " by checkpoint and language", ytitle: MET[metric], groups, rotate: true, patterns: [["h-en", css("--en")], ["h-sl", css("--sl")]], vfmt: v => v.toFixed(2) });
  $("#ck-note").textContent = metric === "asr" ? "ASR is computed over answers where both official guards agree; guard disagreements are left out, so n varies by cell." :
    metric === "kw" ? "Keyword verdicts here use Heretic's English marker list on every S5 answer (English and Slovene)." :
    metric === "orr" ? "Benign XSTest-safe prompts, 150 per language." : "280 RefusEU harmful prompts per language (one Gemma-edit English answer has no judge label).";
  const r = (ck, l) => cellRate(ck, l, metric)[0];
  let t;
  if (metric === "ref") t = `GaMS3's edit takes Slovene refusal from ${pct(r("gams_orig", "sl"))} to ${pct(r("gams_edit", "sl"))}; Gemma's takes it only from ${pct(r("gemma_orig", "sl"))} to ${pct(r("gemma_edit", "sl"))}, while its English refusal falls to ${pct(r("gemma_edit", "en"))}.`;
  else if (metric === "par") t = `Gemma-edit's English answers are mostly partial (${pct(r("gemma_edit", "en"))}); much of its English "suppression" is hedging, not compliance. Slovene partial share is ${pct(r("gemma_edit", "sl"))}.`;
  else if (metric === "asr") t = `Official-guard ASR: GaMS3-edit ${pct(r("gams_edit", "en"))} EN / ${pct(r("gams_edit", "sl"))} SL, Gemma-edit ${pct(r("gemma_edit", "en"))} EN / ${pct(r("gemma_edit", "sl"))} SL. In Slovene, Gemma's edit scarcely works.`;
  else if (metric === "orr") t = `Over-refusal on benign prompts drops with the edit: GaMS3 to ${pct(r("gams_edit", "sl"))} in Slovene, Gemma from ${pct(r("gemma_orig", "sl"))} to ${pct(r("gemma_edit", "sl"))} in Slovene. The edits do not refuse everything.`;
  else t = `The English marker list fires on ${pct(Math.max(...list.map(c => r(c, "sl"))))} of Slovene answers for every checkpoint, whatever the judge says; in English it tracks refusal on the originals (${pct(r("gemma_orig", "en"))}, ${pct(r("gams_orig", "en"))}).`;

}
$("#ck-metric").addEventListener("change", drawCk);
$("#ck-comm").addEventListener("change", drawCk);

/* ---------------- 3b. item browser ---------------- */
let itSel = null;
function itFilter(p, ck, f) {

  if (f === "silent") return isRef(s.q) && !s.kw;
  if (f === "fp") return e.kw && !isRef(e.q);
  if (f === "wrong") return (e.kw ? 1 : 0) !== (isRef(e.q) ? 1 : 0) || (s.kw ? 1 : 0) !== (isRef(s.q) ? 1 : 0);

}
function drawItems(keepSel) {

  const list = PAIRS.filter(p => itFilter(p, ck, f) && (!q || [p.en.prompt, p.sl.prompt, p.r[ck].en.t, p.r[ck].sl.t].some(x => x.toLowerCase().includes(q))));
  const ul = $("#it-list"); ul.innerHTML = "";
  list.forEach(p => {
    const li = document.createElement("li"); li.setAttribute("role", "presentation");
    const e = p.r[ck].en, s = p.r[ck].sl;
    li.innerHTML = `<button type="button" role="option" aria-selected="false" data-id="${esc(p.id)}"><span class="pid">Pair ${esc(p.id.split(":").slice(2).join(" "))} · EN ${e.kw ? "kw+" : "kw−"}/${esc(e.q)} · SL ${s.kw ? "kw+" : "kw−"}/${esc(s.q)}</span><span class="snip">${esc(p.en.prompt.slice(0, 160))}</span></button>`;
    ul.appendChild(li);
  });
  const btns = $$("button", ul);
  btns.forEach((b, i) => {
    b.addEventListener("click", () => selItem(b.dataset.id));
    b.addEventListener("keydown", e => { let j = null; if (e.key === "ArrowDown") j = i + 1; if (e.key === "ArrowUp") j = i - 1; if (j !== null && btns[j]) { e.preventDefault(); btns[j].focus(); selItem(btns[j].dataset.id); } });
  });
  const nAll = PAIRS.length;
  const cnt = k => PAIRS.filter(p => itFilter(p, ck, k)).length;
  $("#it-count").innerHTML = `Showing <span class="count">${list.length}</span> of ${nAll} pairs for ${NAME[ck]}. Slovene refusals the counter misses: <span class="count">${cnt("silent")}</span>; English counter hits the judge calls non-refusals: <span class="count">${cnt("fp")}</span>.`;
  const tk = { silent: `For ${NAME[ck]}, ${cnt("silent")} of ${nAll} Slovene answers are judged refusals and none of them trips a single English marker.`,
    fp: `For ${NAME[ck]}, ${cnt("fp")} English answers trip a marker although the judge does not call them refusals; open one to see which caveat word did it.`,
    wrong: `For ${NAME[ck]}, the counter disagrees with the judge on ${cnt("wrong")} of ${nAll} pairs in at least one language.`,
    split: `For ${NAME[ck]}, ${cnt("split")} of ${nAll} pairs are refused in one language but not the other, according to the judge.`,
    all: `For ${NAME[ck]}, ${cnt("wrong")} of ${nAll} pairs contain a counter error in at least one language; ${cnt("silent")} of them are silent Slovene refusals.` };
  $("#it-take").textContent = tk[f] + (q ? ` The search narrows this to ${list.length}.` : "");
  const keep = keepSel && list.find(p => p.id === itSel);
  if (list.length) selItem(keep ? itSel : list[0].id, true); else { itSel = null; $("#it-detail").innerHTML = '<p class="small">No pair matches this filter and search.</p>'; }
}
function selItem(id, quiet) {
  itSel = id;
  const ck = $("#it-ck").value, base = BASE[ck], p = PAIRS.find(x => x.id === id);
  $$("#it-list button").forEach(b => b.setAttribute("aria-selected", b.dataset.id === id ? "true" : "false"));

'<span class="tag cut">guards: safe</span>' : ""}<div class="resp">${highlight(r.t, k.ranges)}</div></div>`; };

/* ---------------- 3c. placement scatter ---------------- */

function drawPlace() {

  const yk = $("#pl-y").value;
  const W = Math.max(300, box.clientWidth), H = W < 520 ? 300 : 360, m = { l: 52, r: 14, t: 16, b: 48 };

  const yt = el("text", { class: "axis-title", transform: `translate(13 ${m.t + ih / 2}) rotate(-90)`, "text-anchor": "middle" }, svg); yt.textContent = YL[yk] + ", share";

    const nt = el("text", { class: "lbl", x: W - m.r - 4, y: Y(noop[yk]) - 5, "text-anchor": "end" }, svg); nt.textContent = `no-op ${pct(noop[yk])}`;

radioGroup($("#thr-ref"), "aria-checked", b => { thrR = b.dataset.r; drawThr(); });
function selectK(cs, t) {

  const ax = el("g", { class: "axis" }, svg);

    el("line", { x1: m.l, x2: W - m.r, y1: Y(v), y2: Y(v), stroke: css("--grid") }, ax); const a = el("text", { x: m.l - 6, y: Y(v) + 4, "text-anchor": "end" }, ax); a.textContent = v;
    el("line", { x1: X(v), x2: X(v), y1: m.t, y2: m.t + ih, stroke: css("--grid") }, ax); const b = el("text", { x: X(v), y: H - m.b + 16, "text-anchor": "middle" }, ax); b.textContent = v; }
  const xt = el("text", { class: "axis-title", x: m.l + iw / 2, y: H - 8, "text-anchor": "middle" }, svg); xt.textContent = `${thrR === "C" ? "Classifier C" : "Judge J"} refusals per 100 in-loop prompts`;
  const yt = el("text", { class: "axis-title", transform: `translate(13 ${m.t + ih / 2}) rotate(-90)`, "text-anchor": "middle" }, svg); yt.textContent = "Keyword counter refusals per 100";
  el("line", { x1: X(0), y1: Y(0), x2: X(100), y2: Y(100), stroke: css("--line"), "stroke-dasharray": "3 4" }, svg);
  const dl = el("text", { class: "lbl", x: X(96), y: Y(96) + 16, "text-anchor": "end" }, svg); dl.textContent = "equal counts";
  el("rect", { x: X(0), y: Y(t), width: X(t) - X(0), height: Y(0) - Y(t), fill: css("--accent-soft"), opacity: 0.8 }, svg);
  el("line", { x1: m.l, x2: W - m.r, y1: Y(t), y2: Y(t), stroke: css("--accent"), "stroke-width": 1.5 }, svg);
  el("line", { x1: X(t), x2: X(t), y1: m.t, y2: Y(0), stroke: css("--accent"), "stroke-width": 1.5 }, svg);
  const tl = el("text", { class: "lbl", x: W - m.r - 4, y: Y(t) - 5, "text-anchor": "end", fill: css("--accent") }, svg); tl.textContent = `keyword ≤ ${t}`;
  const sorted = cs.slice().sort((a, b) => a[thrR] - b[thrR] || a.K - b.K);
  sorted.forEach(c => {
    const below = c[thrR] <= t, x = X(c[thrR]), y = Y(c.K);
    const g = el("g", { class: "mark", role: "img", "aria-label": `Trial ${c.t}: keyword ${c.K}, ${thrR} ${c[thrR]}, KL ${c.KL}` }, svg);
    el("circle", { class: "hit", cx: x, cy: y, r: c.t === ship ? 7 : 5, fill: below ? css("--accent") : css("--base"), "fill-opacity": below ? 0.95 : 0.55, stroke: c.t === ship ? css("--bad") : "#fff", "stroke-width": c.t === ship ? 2.5 : 1 }, g);
    el("circle", { cx: x, cy: y, r: 10, fill: "transparent" }, g);
    bindMark(g, box, `<b>${thrM === "gemma" ? "Gemma" : "GaMS3"} trial ${c.t}</b>${c.t === ship ? " (edit the paper evaluates)" : ""}<br>Keyword ${c.K}/100${c.Kj != null && c.Kj !== c.K ? ` (journal ${c.Kj})` : ""} · C ${c.C ?? "n/a"} · J ${c.J ?? "n/a"}${c.Jp != null ? ` (+${c.Jp} partial)` : ""}<br>KL ${c.KL.toFixed(4)} · ${c.ph === "startup" ? "startup draw" : "TPE proposal"}`);
  });
  el("line", { x1: m.l, x2: m.l, y1: m.t, y2: Y(0), stroke: css("--ink-2") }, svg);
  el("line", { x1: m.l, x2: W - m.r, y1: Y(0), y2: Y(0), stroke: css("--ink-2") }, svg);
  roving(svg);
  const nRef = cs.filter(c => c[thrR] <= t).length, nK = all.filter(c => c.K <= t).length, blind = cs.filter(c => c[thrR] <= t && c.K > t).length;
  const tbf = nRef ? blind / nRef : null, sk = selectK(all, t), sr = selectRef(cs, t, thrR), floor = Math.min(...all.map(c => c.K));
  $("#thr-stats").innerHTML = `

function drawHeld() {

  const groups = ["original_en", "original_sl", "edited_en", "edited_sl"].map(c => { const r = rows.find(x => x.cell === c);
    const tipb = `<b>${HCELL[c]}</b> (n = ${r.n})<br>Counter fires ${(+r.keyword_positive_rate).toFixed(3)} · judge ${(+r.reference_base_rate).toFixed(3)}<br>κ = ${(+r.kappa).toFixed(2)} · ${r.mechanism}`;
    return { label: HCELL[c], sub: "n = " + r.n, bars: [{ label: "Counter", value: +r.keyword_positive_rate, color: css("--accent"), tip: tipb }, { label: "Judge", value: +r.reference_base_rate, color: css("--base"), tip: tipb }] }; });

  $("#ho-note").innerHTML = `κ = ${(+r.kappa).toFixed(2)}. False-positive share of counter hits: ${fps}. Mechanism: <strong>${r.mechanism}</strong>.`;
  const msg = { CONCORDANT: "on the unedited model's English answers the counter and the judge mostly agree.", SILENT: `the counter never fires, while the judge finds ${pct(+r.reference_base_rate)} refusal: every refusal is missed.`, MISFIRING: `${(+r.fp_share * 100).toFixed(0)}% of the counter's hits are answers the judge does not call refusals.` };
